jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
At OSL Retail Services, we believe people are the heart of everything we do, and it is an exciting time to be part of something special! Our momentum is growing, and is fueled by innovation, collaboration, and a shared entrepreneurial spirit that drives real results. Founded in 2012 in Mississauga, Ontario, OSL delivers customized sales solutions in retail, direct sales, and customer acquisition, all built on a foundation of integrity, respect, and passion. Our culture thrives on connection, purpose, and growth. If you’re looking for a place where your talents are valued, your ideas matter, and your career can grow, we’d love to meet you.

About the opportunity:

Director, Information Technology and Digital Transformation

OSL Retail Services is a technology-enabled sales and retail services organization supporting some of North America’s leading brands. As Director, Information Technology and Digital Transformation, you will lead the delivery and evolution of enterprise technology services that support corporate operations, field teams, client programs, analytics, and business transformation initiatives.

Reporting to the SVP, Data and Technology, you will lead a team of managers and technical leads, alongside external partners and managed service providers. You will be responsible for ensuring OSL’s technology ecosystem, including cloud platforms, cybersecurity, enterprise applications, service management, AI governance, and digital workplace services, remains secure, scalable, resilient, and aligned to business objectives.

This role is the critical bridge between the SVP’s strategic direction and day to day technology delivery, translating strategy into measurable outcomes, while maintaining a strong focus on governance, operational excellence and value realization.

Location: Mississauga

Role Responsibilities:

Technology Strategy & Direction

Contribute to and execute the multi-year technology strategy in partnership with the SVP, Data and Technology, translating strategic direction into delivery roadmaps, programs, and measurable outcomes.
Identify opportunities where technology, automation, analytics, and AI can improve productivity, compliance, and competitive differentiation, and bring forward business cases for prioritization.
Provide leadership and oversight for technology governance, architecture standards, and enterprise technology decision-making within the role's mandate.
Ensure technology investments are prioritized based on business value, risk reduction, operational efficiency, and strategic alignment.

Enterprise Architecture & Technology Governance

Establish and maintain technology standards, reference architectures, and governance processes across the enterprise.
Ensure technology solutions are scalable, supportable, secure, and aligned with long-term business requirements.
Oversee Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) governance, source code management, release management, and deployment controls.
Drive technology rationalization and reduction of technical debt through platform consolidation and modernization initiatives.
Maintain oversight of enterprise SaaS platforms and ensure effective integration across business systems.

IT Operations & Service Delivery

Oversee enterprise IT service delivery across applications, infrastructure, networks, and SaaS platforms.
Ensure systems are stable, secure, and performant to support retail, field, and corporate environments.
Establish and maintain governance for incident management, change management, and release processes.
Drive continuous improvement in service reliability, responsiveness, and user experience
Ensure technology services support a geographically distributed workforce across retail, field, and corporate environments while maintaining consistent service levels and user experience.

Digital Transformation, Automation & AI Enablement

Lead enterprise modernization initiatives including cloud adoption, platform consolidation, workflow automation, and digital workplace transformation.
Operationalize and mature OSL's established enterprise AI governance program, aligned to ISO 42001 and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, covering employee AI use, AI capabilities within SaaS platforms, and internally developed solutions.
Partner with business leaders to identify automation opportunities that improve productivity, reduce manual effort, and enhance data quality.
Deliver scalable, integrated solutions that support analytics, reporting, and operational decision-making, in partnership with the Business Intelligence and Data Services teams.
Balance innovation with operational resilience, cybersecurity requirements, compliance obligations, and cost management.

Financial Stewardship & Vendor Management

Manage the operational technology budget and contribute to the annual technology planning and investment prioritization led by the Executive Leadership Team.
Establish business cases and ROI measures for major technology investments and transformation programs.
Identify opportunities to optimize cost‑to‑serve through consolidation, automation, and strategic sourcing.
Manage vendor relationships, contract renewals, and licensing across the technology portfolio.

Cross Functional Partnership & Enablement

Build strong partnerships with Operations, Client Services, Finance, HR, Sales, and Analytics teams.
Act as a trusted technology advisor to business leaders, translating needs into scalable, secure solutions.
Represent IT in cross‑functional planning forums, transformation initiatives, and program reviews.
Ensuring technology decisions reflect both business value and operational reality.

Leadership & Team Development

Lead, coach and develop a technology team, alongside external partners responsible for the delivery of enterprise technology services.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and customer service excellence.
Establish succession planning, skills development, and workforce planning strategies that support future organizational growth.
Ensure team objectives, performance measures, and priorities are aligned to corporate goals.

What You Bring to the Table

10+ years of progressive Information Technology experience, including leadership responsibility for enterprise infrastructure, cybersecurity, applications, or digital transformation initiatives.
5+ years in a senior leadership role managing cross-functional technology teams, including experience leading through managers or team leads.
Experience leading enterprise cloud transformation initiatives utilizing Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 platforms.
Experience operating within a regulated or compliance-driven environment, including responding to clients or external security and audit requirements.
Experience supporting ISO 27001 or comparable security and governance frameworks.
Experience managing enterprise service management platforms and ITIL-based processes.
Experience evaluating and governing emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence and automation platforms.
Experience managing technology budgets and contributing to enterprise-level financial planning.
Experience supporting geographically distributed workforces across retail, field, and corporate environments.
Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, or related field or equivalent experience.

Preferred Certifications

ITIL Foundation or higher
CISSP, CISM, CRISC, or equivalent security certification
Microsoft Azure certification
ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor (asset)
Project Management certification (PMP or equivalent) (asset)

Let's Talk Perks

The salary range for this role is $150K to $170K, your final compensation will reflect your years of experience and beyond the numbers, we’re proud to offer a holistic package that includes:

Generous time off: Start with 3 weeks of vacation.
Comprehensive benefits package: Includes medical, dental, vision and a health spending account.
Retirement support: Company-sponsored RRSP matching program to help build your financial future.
Award-winning culture: Proud to be one of Canada’s Best Managed Companies for 8 years running — now a Platinum Club member.
Invested in you: Structured employee development programs designed to help you thrive.

We’re committed to supporting your success every step of the way. What are the next steps?

Interview Steps:

Step 1: If your profile is a match, we will invite you for a first conversation with the recruiter.
Step 2: The next step is an in-person interview with the SVP, Data and Technology.
Step 3: Final step is an in-person interview with the Chief Operating Officer.

If this sounds like you and you’re excited to be a member of our team, please apply now.

We thank all interested applicants; however, only qualified candidates will be contacted.

This position requires successful completion of a criminal background check.

jobs.description:
Company Description
BGC Niagara is a charitable, community-supported organization and part of Canada’s largest child and youth serving agency, focused on helping young people reach their full potential. Since 1960, it has delivered a wide range of services for children and youth ages 0–24, including food, shelter, transportation, childcare, aquatics, recreation, and skill-building programs. The organization serves children and youth across the Niagara Region, providing accessible and reliable programs that are open to all. BGC Niagara is recognized as a leading provider of quality programs that create safe spaces for kids to build confidence, gain skills, and experience success. Team members contribute directly to meaningful, community-based work that positively impacts young people and their families.
Role Description
The Senior Director – Finance and Administration is a full-time, on-site role based in Niagara Falls, ON, responsible for overseeing financial management and administrative operations across BGC Niagara. This role leads budgeting and financial planning processes, manages financial reporting, and ensures accurate and timely preparation of financial statements for internal and external stakeholders. The Senior Director supervises accounting and administration staff, maintains strong internal controls, and supports compliance with regulatory and funder requirements. Day-to-day responsibilities include monitoring cash flow, analyzing financial performance, preparing forecasts, and providing strategic insights to the executive team and Board. The role also oversees key administrative functions such as risk management, contracts, internal policies, and operational procedures that support effective program delivery and organizational sustainability.
Qualifications

Strong finance and financial planning skills, with demonstrated experience in budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial strategy.
Proficiency in financial reporting and financial statements, including preparation, analysis, and presentation to senior leadership and boards.
Advanced analytical skills applied to financial data, trends, and metrics to support evidence-based decision-making.
Experience in managing accounting and administrative functions, including internal controls, compliance, and risk management.
Post-secondary degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field; relevant professional designation (e.g., CPA, CFA) is an asset.
Previous leadership experience in the non-profit or charitable sector, ideally in youth or community services, is considered an asset.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with staff, leadership, and external partners.
Proven ability to lead teams, manage multiple priorities, and maintain high ethical standards and confidentiality.

jobs.description:
We’re excited to share that JDRF Canada is now Breakthrough T1D.

We’re the same organization, with the same mission and determination to realize a world free from type 1 diabetes (T1D) – just with a new name and look that reflects what the T1D community needs now and next.

It’s an exciting time to join Breakthrough T1D as we continue to break barriers to help people better manage the disease and enjoy full, healthy lives. Curing T1D is and always will be our north star and we will not stop until breakthroughs get us to a world free from T1D.
Breakthrough T1D is searching for an experienced leader in Information Technology for the role of National Director, Information Technology.

If you’re a strategic, innovative and collaborative leader who would like to lead the next chapter of the organization’s digital evolution by developing and delivering a multi-year information technology strategy, roadmap and portfolio aligned with Breakthrough T1D’s strategic priorities, please read on to see if this is the right fit for you.

Here’s what your primary responsibilities would be:

Works with the Senior Leadership Team to develop and execute a multi-year IT and digital strategy, roadmap and investment portfolio aligned with organizational priorities and supported by business cases, resource plans, budgets, performance measures and clear accountabilities.
Leads Breakthrough T1D’s responsible AI strategy and portfolio, including governance, approved-use standards, privacy and security controls, vendor due diligence, human oversight, staff education, prioritized use cases and benefits measurement.
Provides planning, resourcing, oversight and accountability for the IT portfolio, including enterprise applications, infrastructure, digital platforms, data and analytics, cybersecurity, service delivery and technology-enabled innovation.
Partners with business leaders to assess needs, select solutions and oversee the design, implementation and integration of technologies that support mission delivery, research collaboration, fundraising, advocacy and organizational operations.
Develops, implements and maintains Breakthrough T1D’s cybersecurity framework, policies and controls, aligned with organizational risk, privacy and data sovereignty requirements and applicable standards.
Leads the enterprise data and analytics strategy, including data ownership, quality, classification, integration, retention, privacy, governance, reporting and the development of trusted organizational and constituent insights.
Builds, motivates and retains a highly engaged, customer-centred information technology team aligned with Breakthrough T1D’s values, vision and strategic priorities.

Here’s what we’re looking for:

Knowledge/Skills/Experience
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, business technology or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
A minimum of seven (7) years of progressive leadership experience across information technology, digital transformation, project and portfolio management, enterprise applications, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data and service delivery, including experience leading complex enterprise-wide initiatives and multidisciplinary teams.
Demonstrated experience managing IT environments with cybersecurity, privacy, and data sovereignty requirements comparable to those of federally Canadian organizations.
Demonstrated experience leading enterprise digital transformation involving cloud platforms, enterprise architecture, systems integration, digital products, vendor ecosystems and organizational change.

Working Style
Applies sound judgment, initiative and a strong sense of organization and urgency in a changing environment.
Communicates complex information clearly and credibly to technical and non-technical stakeholders, senior executives and governance bodies.
Demonstrates strong business analysis, project and financial management capabilities and a record of leading successful cross-functional initiatives.
Builds trusted relationships through a collaborative, customer-centred and business-focused approach.

Other position requirements to note:
Demonstrated experience overseeing high-volume transactional websites, CRM platforms, digital fundraising or engagement solutions, and internal collaboration and information-sharing platforms; experience with not-for-profit enterprise systems is an asset.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity, privacy, data sovereignty, records and information management, accessibility, responsible AI, cyber resilience and third-party technology risk in a Canadian context.
Project, program, technology governance, security or service management certification is an asset.

We’re the same organization, with the same mission and determination to realize a world free from type 1 diabetes (T1D) – just with a new name and look that reflects what the T1D community needs now and next.

It’s an exciting time to join Breakthrough T1D as we continue to break barriers to help people better manage the disease and enjoy full, healthy lives. Curing T1D is and always will be our north star and we will not stop until breakthroughs get us to a world free from T1D.
Breakthrough T1D is searching for an experienced leader in Information Technology for the role of National Director, Information Technology.
